project.title: Functional gene annotation and degradation characteristics of plastic-degrading bacteria in activated sludge
project.description: Microbial degradation of plastics is considered to be one of the important ways to alleviate plastic pollution and achieve sustainable development. Due to the lack of systematic studies on the degradation of polystyrene (PS) and polylactic acid (PLA) plastics in activated sludge, experiments were conducted using activated sludge as a microbial source. After 33-day incubation with microbial strains, polystyrene (PS) in the PS-F-2-4 group showed a 2.42% mass loss, while polylactic acid (PLA) and polyethylene (PE) exhibited no detectable mass loss. Scanning electron microscopy observation showed that there was obvious biofilm adhesion on the plastic surface, and grooves and cracks appeared on the surface after cleaning, and the water contact angle test showed that the hydrophilicity of the plastic surface was enhanced, which was conducive to microbial colonization. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy and X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy analyses further confirmed the formation of new oxygen-containing functional groups (e.g., hydroxyl, carbonyl, ester groups) on the surface of plastics, and a significant increase in O/C ratio, providing direct evidence of microbial degradation. In addition, this study combining pure culture techniques with metagenomic sequencing, the functional genes of degrading bacteria were annotated, which revealed the abundance and metabolic pathway of the strain-encoding plastic-degrading enzyme, and elucidated the potential mechanism of the strain's degradation of plastics. This study provides an important theoretical basis for in-depth exploration of the degradation and metabolism mechanisms of PLA, PE and PS plastics in the environment.
